title: The backend list is effectively immutable in production, because adding or removing a switchboard remaps about 1/N of documents with no migration story
content:
This is named as **the biggest operational sharp edge of the MVP**, in the architecture document and again in the repo's `CLAUDE.md` so it is not forgotten.

`hash $doc_id consistent` is Ketama-style consistent hashing across the `server` entries, so:

- **adding** a backend remaps ~1/N of documents — the same fundamental tradeoff any stateless scheme has — and until `switchboard` supports migration this is a coordinated maintenance event, not a self-serve operation;
- **removing** a backend makes the documents pinned to it **unroutable**, under the same rule.

The long-term fix is acknowledged and deferred: an explicit `doc_id → backend` **directory** (Redis or Postgres) so adding a backend does not remap anything. It requires coordinated migration support in `switchboard`, which does not exist — recorded as open question 4, "how do operators migrate a document between backends?", cross-cutting `switchboard` and `reactor`, to be decided *before operating this at any meaningful scale*.

Reload itself is safe and uses nginx's own mechanics: master parses the new config and old workers keep running if it fails; on success new workers start, old workers finish in-flight requests and exit, zero dropped connections. `scripts/reload.sh` wraps `nginx -t` then `nginx -s reload` and fails loudly if validation fails. A long-lived WebSocket survives a reload because old workers drain gracefully — proven by an integration test that opens a real WS, reloads mid-flight and asserts both the connection and a frame round-trip survive.
